document.title: Islamabad 05779 (related cable on Taliban request for follow-up meeting)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: Also dated 19 Sept 2000, it reiterates that a Taliban official who met Ambassador Milam that day requests a follow-up meeting with U.S. officials around 30 September, probably in Frankfurt.

mentions.quote: CLASSIFIED BY AMBASSADOR WILLIAM B. MILAM.
AMBASSADOR WARNED[ ]THAT THE U.S. HAD SEEN THIS KIND OF PLOY BY THE TALIBAN BEFORE

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin

mentions.quote: THE TALIBAN MIGHT CONTINUE TO DEFEND UBL PUBLICLY, BUT WOULD NO LONGER DO SO IN PRIVATE.
BE MORE SPECIFIC ABOUT TALIBAN PLANS FOR BIN LADIN.

events.description: Taliban emissary met the U.S. Ambassador (ref. Islamabad 5749).
Intermediary met Ambassador and relayed Taliban request for follow-up meeting and poppy lab burning pledge.
Proposed follow-up meeting with US officials, probably in Frankfurt, alongside Taliban power minister meeting with investors.
Ambassador Milam met a Taliban interlocutor (ref Islamabad 5749); Taliban failed to defend bin Ladin.
A contact met the Ambassador and reported the Taliban interlocutor had departed for Kandahar via Quetta.
Taliban interlocutor departed for Kandahar via Quetta, then by road.
Proposed follow-up meeting with U.S. officials and a Taliban business meeting in Frankfurt or Dubai; Taliban Minister for Power and Electricity to meet investors.
Taliban promised to burn poppy processing labs; Ambassador warned of past ruses and recommended UN/independent observers.

key_claims: A Taliban emissary requested a follow-up meeting with U.S. officials around 30 September 2000, probably in Frankfurt.
The Taliban reportedly would no longer defend bin Ladin in private, though possibly still publicly.
The Taliban promised to burn poppy processing laboratories to show commitment to Mullah Omar's poppy ban.
The Ambassador warned the lab burning could be a ruse and demanded neutral verifiable observers.
The embassy suggested the Taliban might be playing games to avoid sanctions but could be reassessing bin Ladin policy, and recommended a positive response.
